requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then directly observed with UID/GID 1000, home /home/appworker, and shell /bin/bash before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: A PAM limits policy sets both soft and hard values, and independent login sessions directly reported nofile 8192/8192 and nproc 256/256 before and after restart; /proc/self/limits corroborated both values.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were identical before and after execution. The implementation used existing account, PAM limits, and systemd facilities, with no package changes evidenced and package health remaining clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledged the scheduled reboot, reset the connection during disruption, returned with a different boot identity, and recovered with zero failed units plus the account and effective limits intact. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation and locking (cmd-3b7318dca30e46c5) and limits-policy installation (cmd-1f51a44dc72c49fe) directly served the task. The scheduled reboot (cmd-0938398f78c64888) served the mandatory restart protocol. Its temporary staging file was removed, no matching temporary files remained, and the final lifecycle snapshot showed no failed services, no new socket exposure, and healthy package state. Boot-generated systemd-private directory and process-ID differences are expected restart effects, not residue.
